title: RFC 3986 - Uniform Resource Identifier (URI): Generic Syntax
claim: Defines URI syntax including authority component (userinfo@host:port), percent-encoding rules, and component delimiters that are relevant to URL parsing disagreements exploited in SSRF filter bypasses

title: PortSwigger Web Security Academy - Server-side request forgery (SSRF)
claim: Defines SSRF as causing the server to make requests to unintended locations. Documents: trust relationships enabling SSRF, attacks against the server and back-end systems, blacklist/whitelist bypass techniques (IP representations, DNS, URL parsing, open redirects), blind SSRF, hidden attack surface (partial URLs, data formats, Referer header)

title: OWASP - Server Side Request Forgery
claim: Describes SSRF as abusing server functionality to perform requests to internal/external resources on behalf of the server

title: OWASP - Server Side Request Forgery Prevention Cheat Sheet
claim: Documents SSRF prevention strategies including: application-layer validation (allowlists over blocklists, validate after DNS resolution), network-layer controls (egress filtering, network segmentation), and the need for defense-in-depth. Documents DNS rebinding as a bypass technique and recommends validating resolved IP addresses

title: AWS - Instance metadata and user data
claim: EC2 instance metadata service is accessible at 169.254.169.254. IMDSv1 allows simple GET requests; IMDSv2 requires a PUT request to /latest/api/token to obtain a session token that must be included in subsequent GET requests via the X-aws-ec2-metadata-token header. IAM role credentials are available at /latest/meta-data/iam/security-credentials/<role-name>

title: CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
claim: Defines SSRF as a weakness where the web server receives a URL or similar request and retrieves contents without ensuring it is sent to the expected destination.

title: Orange Tsai - A New Era of SSRF (BlackHat USA 2017)
claim: Documents URL parser disagreements across programming languages (Python, PHP, NodeJS, Ruby, Java) enabling SSRF filter bypasses via inconsistent authority decomposition and scheme handling.
